title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty of Work in Time-Dependently Driven Open Quantum Systems
abstract: We derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation for work in an open quantum system driven by a time-dependent protocol and subject to repeated projective energy measurements. The protocol is represented by a sequence of protocol quenches separated by finite-time Lindblad evolution, so that work is accumulated at the quenches while dissipation occurs between them. The resulting work statistics obey the Gallavotti-Cohen symmetry to give rise to the Crooks and Jarzynski fluctuation relations. By perturbing the dissipative dynamics and combining the Cramér--Rao inequality with the quantum Fisher information, we obtain $\mathrm{Var}\,{\cal W}/[τ\partial_τ\langle{\cal W}\rangle]^2\ge 1/{\cal F}\ge\max(1/{\cal A},2/{\cal E})$, where $\langle{\cal W}\rangle$ is the work expectation value, $\mathrm{Var}\,{\cal W}$ is the variance of work, ${\cal F}$ is the Fisher information, ${\cal A}$ is the dynamical activity, ${\cal E}$ is the dimensionless entropy production, and $τ$ is the switching time interval between quenches. The two thermodynamic bounds follow from two independent perturbations that generate the same response of the work statistics. We illustrate the relation for a dissipative two-level system under square-wave and sinusoidal driving and show that the tighter thermodynamic bound can depend on the driving protocol and switching time scale.
summary: This paper derives a novel thermodynamic uncertainty relation for the work done in an open quantum system driven by time-dependent protocols. By combining the Cramér–Rao inequality with quantum Fisher information, the authors establish a bound relating the work variance to the system's dynamical activity and entropy production. This result provides a quantitative measure of non-equilibrium fluctuations in quantum thermodynamics.
main_problem: The paper derives a thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR) for the work done in an open quantum system subjected to time-dependent driving and repeated energy measurements.

method: The analysis combines the Cramér–Rao inequality with the quantum Fisher information by perturbing the dissipative dynamics, leveraging the system's adherence to fluctuation theorems.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the framework by noting that work statistics obey fluctuation relations. It then applies estimation theory, using two independent perturbations to derive the core uncertainty relation, which is finally illustrated using specific two-level system examples (square-wave and sinusoidal driving).
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, quantitative bound on the fluctuations of work in non-equilibrium quantum processes, extending fluctuation theorems into the realm of quantum estimation theory, which is highly relevant for quantum thermodynamics.
